subject: Observability integration for private deployment — log & trace export options
messages:

Cc: Tom Hayes <tom.hayes@acme.com>

Subject: Observability integration for private deployment — log/tracing export requirements

Hi Naomi / Marcus,

Thanks for taking this on. We're preparing the private deployment in our AWS account (us-west-2) and need a clear pattern for getting logs and traces into our internal Splunk/SIEM stack while satisfying our security constraints. A few hard requirements from security: 

- No outbound traffic to public internet from the inference subnet (approved egress only via approved NAT gateways or PrivateLink endpoints).
- SIEM ingestion must use TLS with client certs (mTLS preferred) or a pre-shared HEC token delivered via secure channel.
- Preferred log format: CEF for events / RFC5424 syslog acceptable as fallback. For traces: OTLP over gRPC to our collector.
- PII redaction rules: remove or hash any fields that match SSN/email patterns before leaving the VPC.
- Retention and audit: we need 12 months of audit logs for access and configuration changes.

Target timeline: target cutover week of 24 Jul; would like a short design + mutual action plan by 12 Jul. Also attaching a sample Splunk ingestion spec (attached to this message).

Can you propose 2-3 deployment patterns we can evaluate (sidecar per runtime, centralized forwarder EC2/EKS daemonset, or managed Transit Gateway with forwarder)? Also call out any infra we will need to provision (NAT, PrivateLink, route tables, IAM roles).

Thanks,
Lina Gomez
Sr. Security Engineer, Acme Corp
security-ops@acme.com

[Attachment: acme-splunk-ingest-spec.pdf (application/pdf)]

Subject: Re: Observability integration for private deployment — log/tracing export options

Lina — thanks, this is very clear. High level we can support three deployment patterns that meet your constraints; below is a concise summary with tradeoffs. I've attached a sample forwarder config and a short question list (siem-handshake-questions.pdf) to finalize details.

Pattern A — Centralized forwarder (recommended for quick rollout)
- Deploy an EKS daemonset or dedicated EC2 autoscaling group in a dedicated telemetry subnet.
- Forwarder (fluentd/otelcol) performs CEF/RFC5424 formatting, PII scrubbing (regex/hashing), and buffers to local disk.
- Egress: allow only to Splunk HEC via PrivateLink or NAT + HEC IPs; mTLS client certs from your PKI.
- Pros: simpler to manage, single place to enforce scrubbing and batching; Cons: single cluster component to scale and secure.

Pattern B — Sidecar per inference node
- Sidecar collector runs with each instance; good for low-latency trace correlation.
- Pros: best per-request correlation and lower intra-VPC traffic; Cons: operational overhead and more certs/keys to manage.

Pattern C — Transit forwarder with VPC peering/Transit Gateway
- Forwarder sits in a centralized logging VPC and receives from inference VPC via VPC peering or TGW.
- Pros: isolates telemetry plane; Cons: requires network/hub architecture changes.

Questions (see attached PDF for details):
- Do you have an existing PrivateLink endpoint for Splunk HEC, or should we design for NAT with IP allowlist?
- Who will manage client cert rotation and where will the private keys live (ACME KMS/HSM)?
- Any existing OTLP sampling policy you'd like us to honor at the collector?

Proposed next step: technical review session (30–45m) Thu 12 Jul 10:00–10:45 PT or Fri 13 Jul 09:00–09:45 PT. After that we'll produce a one-page mutual action checklist and a forwarder config you can validate.

Attachments: forwarder-config-example.yaml, siem-handshake-questions.pdf

Best,

Subject: Re: Observability integration for private deployment — log/tracing export options

Naomi / Lina — following up with a concise technical sketch for the centralized forwarder (Pattern A) and the tracing hook approach. Below are config snippets and operational notes.

--- forwarder config (otelcol/fluentd hybrid) ---
- listeners: syslog (RFC5424) on 1514/tcp, otlp on 4317
- processors: regex-based processors that run a PII redaction pipeline (order: redact SSN -> hash emails -> drop raw headers)
- exporters: splunk_hec (endpoint: https://splunk-hec-private.acme.internal:8088, auth: client-cert + token)
- buffering: file buffer 4GB, retry initial backoff 2s -> 1m, max retries 10

Notes on network & auth:
- Use a PrivateLink/Lambda-backed NLB in front of Splunk if you can expose a PrivateLink — this avoids NAT egress.
- If PrivateLink is not possible, HEC IP allowlist + NAT instance is acceptable; make sure egress is restricted to HEC IPs and ports.
- mTLS: forwarder will present a client cert from Redwood (or ACME-provisioned cert); mutual auth verified by Splunk.

Tracing hooks & sampling:
- For traces, we recommend local sampling at SDK level (default 5%) and another sampler in the collector to drop noisy spans (healthchecks, heartbeat).
- Add a trace_id tag to logged events at the runtime layer to improve joinability between logs and spans.
- For high-volume endpoints, enable tail-based sampling in otelcol (requires buffering capacity; plan for 100–200MB buffer per collector pod).

Operational checklist excerpt:
- Confirm PrivateLink vs NAT
- Cert management: who issues and rotates client certs
- Retention window for forwarded logs in Splunk (we will keep local disk buffer for 72h)
- Alerting: configure collector-level alerts for exporter failure, disk pressure, and high retry rates

I'll bring a preliminary OTEL collector manifest to the call.

— Marcus
Marcus Lin
